synthesis.body: A criterion that asserts a property of the code's character instead of naming an input and an observable gives a reviewer nothing to test. Phrasings like "writability is a filesystem fact", "exclusion is structural", "the record is revalidated in full", or "no module reads the clock" draw the correct reviewer answer "names no mechanism"; the author then adds prose, and that prose becomes the next round's surface. Measured on one spec-stage loop: round one produced 36 findings across two reviewers, and round two produced 43 more, of which 33 were caused by round one's own remedies. Write each criterion as: given this concrete input, this exact observable - a published refusal code, a field value, a byte comparison, or an enumerated symbol set over an enumerated path. Naming a refusal code in a criterion is an outcome, not leaked mechanism; the line is observable-versus-implementation, not detail-versus-prose. Rewriting on that rule cut median criterion length from 71 words to 38, removed every compound criterion, and independently covered four of the five blockers the next adjudication sustained.

title: An acceptance criterion asserting the code's character is unfalsifiable and compounds review churn
